questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nature, outdoor activities, being able to do classes within my field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great time!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation days, lots of emails, office hours (that I didn't use), zoom meetings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I tried from home and didn't find any, so ended up booking a hostel for my first week in vic, while I was looking for a place to stay. I found a good place very quickly once I was there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked it, but make sure you are somewhat close to busses or have a bike :) Everyone I talked to found a place before classes started, so don't stress too much, you'll find a good place for sure! (there is a housing crisis in vic so housing isn't super easy to find, but also not harder than in other cities I've lived in, in my opinion.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that much help from uvic with housing. Some exchange students stayed on campus and that was fine as well though :)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you have to prove that you have the right level to do a course and then you get an assigned time to sign up for courses. It's easy to change courses or drop them in the first couple of weeks of the semester, so don't stress too much. On the other hand some courses will fill up quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lots of help! zoom guides, office hours, emails. Almost too much help haha ;)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to look at courses you can't do at home. I did pottery which was a nice break from studying.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked my classes, but academic level really depends on what courses/levels you choose.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very mixed, but the biggest difference was many small assignments throughout the semester makes up your grade. I didn't wanna overburden myself with studying so didn't take too hard courses, but learned really cool things.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Varied greatly from class to class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AE303a Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques	
Es 240 Ecological Processes	
Es 321 Ethnoecology
GEOG 309 Geography of British Columbia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved ethnoecology as I learned a lot about indigenous peoples and the history of vancouver island and current contemporary conflicts. Also liked doing ceramics! And my other two classes were nice but sometimes almost too easy, but I still learned a lot so I was happy I choose them.

questions.answer: Whitewater club! Ecological restoriation club events!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everything outdoors. So many hikes, and places to camp :) Loved the island!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I don't know. Talk to people in class maybe.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outdoor culture!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sign up for clubs or sports! Don't study too much, priorities doing trips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about a new place, culture, worldview. And going on hiking/camping/kayak/canoing/surfing trips.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: 4 months is weird amount of time to be somewhere because it is both very long and very short.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
